quote: until I saw that it was embarrassingly obvious
content: The criterion in the essay is not the feeling; it is stated two paragraphs later as the ability to put in numbers and get out anticipations. "Embarrassingly obvious" describes the moment a derivation closed, and the derivation is checkable by anyone. The illusion-of-explanatory-depth literature’s own remedy is to ask the person to produce the explanation, which is exactly the test the essay is recommending and passing (Rozenblit & Keil 2002). An essay that reports a feeling and the derivation that caused it has supplied more than a report.

quote: putting in numbers and getting out results that control your anticipation of particular experiences
content: The Force Concept Inventory is cited here against the criterion it implements. Its items are qualitative anticipation questions — where will the ball land, which way does the force point — and they are used precisely because they cannot be answered by symbol manipulation. Students who fail it are students whose equations do not control their expectations about particular experiences, which is the essay’s definition of a password verbatim (Hestenes, Wells & Swackhamer 1992). The essay is not praising computation; the sentence quoted requires the numbers to come out as anticipations of what you will see.

quote: which must be the correct answer because the teacher heard a physicist emit the same sound-vibrations
content: The essay agrees that testimony is evidence and says so in the sequence’s treatment of what evidence is; its complaint is not that the student believed the physicist. It is that "light is waves" then controlled no expectation whatever — the student could not say what a wave does, could not predict interference, and would have accepted "light is particles" with equal facility had the teacher emitted those vibrations instead. A belief acquired by testimony and connected to anticipations is knowledge; the same words with nothing attached are the password. The essay’s test distinguishes them, and it is not a test about derivation from first principles.
